purpose: Record two operator rulings verbatim, because both constrain how later text may be written.

the_numbers.assessment: a narrow miss, NOT a clean separation
the_numbers.consequence: with a larger item count gpt2 would quite possibly cross the ceiling

ruling_1_the_negative_control_is_clean_o.limitation_text_recorded_verbatim: The non-significance of the negative control gpt2 is POWER-DEPENDENT and must not be read as 'gpt2 has no readout'. The OA-004 diagnosis already established that gpt2 reads at about 390 times the chance rate. Its role in this study is as a descriptive control, and its non-significance does not constitute evidence of 'no workspace'. The real null is carried by the random-lens null, whose readout is essentially zero and which is clean.

ruling_2_the_eq1_boundary.the_only_permitted_consequence_of_the_co: an INTERPRETIVE FOOTNOTE: the convention V that EQ1 used has no overlap with the rank-derived band, so EQ1's FAIL is attributable to EQ1's implementation choice rather than to a property of the model.
ruling_2_the_eq1_boundary.explicitly_forbidden_verbatim: It is forbidden to restart any part of EQ1 on the grounds that re-running it under convention D might PASS. EQ1's FAIL is an accomplished fact about that execution of ours.
ruling_2_the_eq1_boundary.why_this_prohibition_matters: re-running a failed measurement under a convention chosen after the failure would convert a recorded result into a search for a passing configuration, which is precisely what the whole registration discipline exists to prevent

ruling_3_dc_005_accepted_with_its_reason.the_adjudication_basis_verbatim: Changing the implementation to match the registered text is a bug fix. Changing the registered text to match the data is p-hacking. The distinguishing feature is the DIRECTION.
ruling_3_dc_005_accepted_with_its_reason.the_supporting_check_accepted: the negative control was clean under both readings, so the correction could not have been rescuing it

claim_ceiling: A record of rulings. It licenses no claim of any kind.
